title: Reverse the Order of Words
statement:
A word is a run of characters that are not spaces. The text s contains at least one word, but spaces may appear anywhere: before the first word, after the last, and several in a row between words.

Return the words in reverse order, joined by exactly one space, with no space at the start or end. The letters inside each word stay as they are.

examples.why: Three words, reversed. The extra spaces at both ends and between words all disappear.
A single word stays the same. Reversing the characters ("olleh") would be wrong.
The double space between b and c becomes a single space in the answer.

constraints: s holds letters, digits, punctuation and ' '
s contains at least one word
hints: First collect the words, ignoring spaces entirely. Then the order is easy to fix.
Walk the string from the end. Skip spaces, then find where the current word starts.
With two indexes, one at the end of the word and one moving left to its start, you can copy each word to the output as you find it.

explain.intuition:
The spaces carry no information: only the words and their order matter. So the job is "find the words, then write them back in reverse". The built-in way is split, drop empty pieces, reverse, join(" "). Interviewers often ask for it by hand.

By hand, scan from the right end. Skip spaces until you hit a character: that is the end of a word. Move a second index left until the next space: that is the start. Copy that slice to the output, add one separator, and keep going. Words come out last-to-first, which is exactly the order you want.
steps: Set i = s.length − 1 and an empty list of words.
Move i left past spaces. If it falls off the start, stop.
Set end = i, then move i left until s[i] is a space or i < 0.
The word is s[i + 1 … end]. Add it to the list and repeat.
Join the list with single spaces.
pitfalls: Splitting on a single space. "a b".split(" ") gives ["a", "", "b"], and the empty piece turns into a double space.
Reversing the characters of the whole string instead of the order of words.
Leaving a space at the end because a separator was added after every word, including the last.

solutions.title: Split, reverse, join
solutions.idea: Split on runs of whitespace, drop the empty pieces, and join the reversed list with single spaces.

solutions.title: Scan from the end with two indexes
solutions.idea: Walk right to left. Skip spaces, mark the end of a word, walk to its start, and emit the slice.

followups: If the string were a mutable character array, how would you do it in O(1) extra space? (Hint: reverse everything, then each word.)
Keep the original spacing between words exactly as it was, only swapping the words. What changes?
